sourceNote: Source: Cybersecurity Bootcamp Outline 2026 Version 1.1.xlsx, Cybersecurity Outline sheet.

warnings.message: Expanded 1040 cells from 136 merged ranges. Date and day are stored once per teaching day in the sheet and were copied onto each session in that merge. No date was invented.
Expanded 27 cells from 7 merged ranges on the outline (title and block labels).
Columns I–K are a daily time template, including Excel time fractions and a Thursday/Friday row labelled Madam Diana. They were not imported as sessions. The Timetable sheet is the daily schedule.
The professionalism trainer cell is blank. No trainer was invented for that week.

These practical rows include a 10-minute break note (3:20–3:30 p.m.) inside the course text. The note is stored on the session. It was not turned into its own row, because the sheet does not give it a separate time slot.
The activity cell is empty. The row is stored as type "event" and the course text is kept. A lesson type was not guessed.

Name variants were folded onto one trainer record: Stanley → Stanley K. Dankyira (3); George Plange → George Edward Plange (22); Madam Diana → Diana van der Stelt (22). Madam Diana follows the outline time-template label and the timetable text. Stanley and George Plange follow the longer names used elsewhere on the same workbook.
Extra spaces in a trainer cell were collapsed before matching. The people were not duplicated.
A slash between names (Arnold/Ken) was treated as two trainers.
TBC and "To be confirmed" were not created as trainer records. The row is marked unconfirmed.
"All" was not created as a trainer. The row is marked as the whole teaching group.
Maxim Nyansa Team is stored as a proposed group label, not as a person and not as a login.

The sheet says proposed trainer groups follow the outline and daily allocation is pending. Week-level trainers come from the outline. Session trainers come from the timetable. Both are stored. They do not always list the same people.
The timetable spells "Inter-School Rebotics Competitions". That spelling was kept. It was not corrected to Robotics.
